subject: Dedicated footprint & warm-up approach for CumulusAI
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@cumulusai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated footprint & warm-up approach for CumulusAI

Alex —

Great speaking this morning. Attached is a concise set of reservation options to support the pilot and an initial production ramp for CumulusAI. High-level summary up front:

- Option A (Conservative): 8x A100-equivalent GPUs baseline, 2x warm-hot GPUs kept online for low-latency control plane, burst to 16 GPUs during working hours via burst credits.
- Option B (Production Ramp): 16x A100-equivalent GPUs baseline, min-kept = 4 GPUs (to keep model cache warm), stepped ramp to 48 GPUs by month 6 (scheduled scale-ups).
- Option C (Aggressive): 32x baseline with autoscale + priority lanes (recommended if 99th p95 latency target <= 120ms and steady-state qps > 200).

Key trade-offs: baseline size controls concurrency and steady-state unit cost; min-kept GPUs determine cache warm retention and cold-start frequency; ramp schedule balances cashflow vs. runway for model optimizations.

I've flagged the two configurations we discussed as most relevant: Option A for a quick, low-commit pilot and Option B for a staged production onboarding with a predictable monthly commitment and warm-up credits. See the attached PDF for the quantitative assumptions (token mix, synthetic qps profile, sample warmup savings).

Next actions I'd propose:
1) You confirm which option aligns with procurement appetite (A or B).
2) If B, we draft a 6-month ramp schedule and set agreed activation windows for burst credits.
3) Marissa to run a short bench (2–3 days) on a mirrored dataset to validate latency/cost assumptions.

I'll leave Marissa copied to coordinate the bench.

Thanks,
Diego
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: 20270903_cumulusai_reservation_options_v1.pdf (PDF, 3 pages)
Attachment: cumulusai_usage_sample.csv (CSV, 120KB)
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@cumulusai.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated footprint & warm-up approach for CumulusAI

Diego —

Thanks for the summary and the options. Quick answers from our side after an internal sync:

- Pilot: We'll aim for Option A to start (fast turn-up). Procurement prefers smaller initial commitment while legal runs a quick review.
- Production intent: We like Option B as a pathway — the min-kept = 4 GPUs aligns with our estimates for keeping the LLM embedding cache warm.
- Question: for Option B, how are warm-up credits applied (do they reduce committed spend in month 1?) and what's the SLA for burst credits during M-F business hours?

Priya (cc'd) will coordinate with procurement on internal approvals. We can carve out a 3-week window next month for Marissa's bench.

Alex
Head of ML Platform
CumulusAI

Alex —

Thanks — I've scheduled a bench slot for 2027-09-20 to 2027-09-22. Plan: we spin up an 8-GPU sandbox that mirrors Option A traffic and a 16-GPU mirror for the Option B steady-state profile. Deliverables at end of run: p50/p95 latency, token cost per 1k, and a short playbook for cache-warm strategies (KV lifetime, prefix-warm job).

Answers to your questions:
- Warm-up credits: For Option B we propose an onboarding credit equal to one week of projected committed spend. That credit is applied to month 1 invoice as a one-time adjustment (reduces month 1 charge). We'll put exact amortization into the draft SOW.
- Burst credits SLA: We'll guarantee 24/7 burst availability subject to fleet capacity in region; for M-F business hours we'll offer higher priority with a 99% availability target on burst activation when within agreed burst windows. Specifics in the SLO appendix.

Ben — can you add the proposed SLO language and an initial cost table into the proposal PDF? Vivek — once procurement signals readiness, we should lock the ramp dates and DocuSign cadence so procurement can align budget quarters.

Cheers,
Marissa
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
